llm.summary: The code implements RunPod image/video functionality and legitimately needs a RunPod API key and (optionally) Cloudflare R2 credentials, but there are metadata mismatches and some surprising assumptions about local secrets and runtime binaries that the user should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The scripts' behavior (calling RunPod endpoints, uploading local files to Cloudflare R2) matches the skill's stated purpose. However the registry metadata shown at the top of the evaluation (no required env vars / no required binaries) is inconsistent with the bundled _meta.json and SKILL.md which explicitly require a RunPod API key and Cloudflare R2 credentials and indicate a dependency on the 'uv' runtime. That mismatch is unexplained and worth caution.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and the scripts explicitly instruct the agent to read ~/.openclaw/secrets.json for /runpod/apiKey and cloudflare.r2 entries and to upload local images by generating R2 presigned URLs, then call RunPod API endpoints. All file and network actions in the instructions are relevant to the declared media-generation purpose; there is no evidence the instructions ask for unrelated system file reads or external endpoints beyond RunPod and Cloudflare.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (script-only), which is lower risk from an arbitrary-download perspective. But the included scripts declare dependencies (requests, boto3) and the wrapper uses 'uv run' — no installer is provided to ensure those binaries/packages exist. _meta.json also lists 'uv' as a required binary. The lack of an explicit install step or dependency manifest means runtime failures or unexpected behavior unless the environment already has the required runtime and Python packages.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests sensitive credentials (RunPod API key and Cloudflare R2 accessKeyId/secretAccessKey/endpoint/bucket) which are proportionate to the features (uploading local files and calling RunPod). Still, the top-level registry summary presented earlier reported 'no required env vars' while bundled metadata and the SKILL.md ask for secrets — this inconsistency is concerning. Also note the scripts read ~/.openclaw/secrets.json directly (and in some helpers parse the whole file), so any secrets stored there are accessible to these scripts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills' or system-wide agent settings. It will write to its own endpoints.json when using the discover_endpoints add command (adding entries under the skill directory), which is reasonable for its purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the RunPod media features it claims — it needs your RunPod API key and, if you want local-file uploads, Cloudflare R2 credentials. Before installing, consider: 1) The published registry metadata (no envs, no bins) disagrees with the bundled SKILL.md and _meta.json — expect to provide secrets and to have the 'uv' runtime plus Python packages (requests, boto3). 2) The scripts read ~/.openclaw/secrets.json; only store credentials there that you are comfortable exposing to this skill. 3) If you prefer not to give Cloudflare R2 credentials, you can host files elsewhere (URLs) or modify the scripts to use a different uploader. 4) Review endpoints.json (included) and be aware discover_endpoints can add entries into the skill folder. If you decide to proceed, provide only the minimum credentials (RUNPOD_API_KEY env var is supported) and consider using short-lived R2 credentials or an isolated account/bucket to limit blast radius.
